answer: The island lists finished tasks with their hashes, and the kernel is where a second reviewer recomputes them. By the pearl of the epoch the only identities still standing are the ones whose work held up. The design leans on session-key rotation bound to work, slashed on a failed audit. Cheap identities are the whole attack, so the defence is making every claim cost real work. Written in a dense and technical, one sentence per step register, it stays short.
